title: Settlement Basis: Lodged Refund Claims on Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
A lodged claim on a booking under Air Ticket Fare Brands settles in the form the fare brand prescribes and in no other form: money to the card, or value on a voucher, never both and never a mixture.

**When it settles.** The settlement takes the brand's processing time, counted in business days from the day the claim was lodged, excluding weekends and public holidays in the traveller's country of residence.

*Worked determination on hypothetical figures.* Take a claim lodged on Thursday 3 September 2026 under a brand carrying a hypothetical processing time of four business days, with no public holiday of the traveller's country of residence falling in the stretch. Four business days are counted from that lodging. The Saturday and the Sunday falling in the stretch are passed over and counted for nothing, as would any public holiday of the traveller's country of residence, so the settlement falls in the week after the one in which the claim was lodged.

**The state a payout requires.** A payout line is raised only while the booking record stands at cancelled, refund pending or refunded. The status is read from the record of the booking the payout would be raised on, before the line is raised.

**Payout lines and the fare lines they reverse.** Each payout line was raised against the original fare line it reverses, so that a booking with several fare lines settled as several payout lines and never as one lump sum; and a payout could never exceed the amount that original line actually collected, nor could the sum of a booking's payouts exceed the amount paid on the booking. Both of those bases are no longer in force. The other clauses of this note stand.

**Where the airline declines.** Where the airline declines the claim, the booking is closed with no payout and the traveller is told which airline reference declined it.

**Where the airline is silent.** A claim that the airline has not answered within the brand's processing time is escalated rather than settled out of agency funds.

A payout may never exceed the amount that original line actually collected, and the sum of a booking's payouts may never exceed the amount paid on the booking.
